newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-GUARANI APPOINT THEIR 10TH COACH OF THE YEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GUARANI APPOINT THEIR 10TH COACH OF THE YEAR.

text.p: Carlos Alberto Silva became Brazilian club Guarani's 10th coach of the year on Thursday.
His predecessor Carbone was still pondering why he had been sacked after only two defeats in his 10-match stay.
Carbone was dismissed by volatile club president Beto Zini on Tuesday after lifting the team from 23rd in the Brazilian championship to their current position of third.
"I nearly fell out of my seat when he (Zini) told me," Carbone said. Silva, returning for his fourth spell at the club, said: "I don't even know why the last one (coach) left."

Carbone, who threatened to take the club to court if they failed to fulfil a verbal agreement to pay three months' wages in compensation, speculated he was sacked for refusing to accept instructions from the president during matches.
"He used a mobile phone to call me on the touchline and give instructions. I told him I did not want this and hung up," said Carbone.
Zini told the Gazeta Esportiva that Carbone had been fired for having a drink with a rival coach following Saturday's 1-0 defeat away to Sport Recife.

"He didn't take seriously instructions he had been given about Sport's team. He lost the game and then went and had a beer with the coach of Sport. I couldn't allow him to behave in that way, as if nothing had happened," said Zini.
Guarani used seven coaches during the Sao Paulo championship, held in the first half of the year, and are now on to their third coach of the Brazilian championship which began in August.
The dismissal was arguably the most bizarre this year in the remarkable world of Brazilian soccer coaching, where the constant chopping and changing is known as "the dance of the coaches".
Eleven of the 24 teams in the Brazilian championship have changed coaches since the competition started.
Parana fired Mario Juliato on Tuesday after just 20 days in charge of their team.
Bahia coach Fito Neves is favourite to be the next victim.
